overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a clear preference for extreme cosmic phenomena, specific 'What If' planetary scenarios, and comparative timeline hooks. Videos focused on unusual space conditions (such as planetary weather anomalies and hypothetical environmental immersion) and surprising biological longevity comparisons generate the strongest view velocities and engagement rates, particularly when leveraging curiosity-gap framing.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') and 8KEl0_pJ_68 ('What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') achieved high view counts (970-1030+ views) with superior like-to-view ratios compared to older straightforward facts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing high-stakes hypothetical planetary survival and environmental immersion scenarios using vivid, tactile adjectives.

winning_patterns.evidence: QXuqYERlqSo ('This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') and v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b') outperformed standard space facts by pairing unusual physical states with strong visual descriptors.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize lesser-known exoplanets with bizarre meteorological or optical properties (e.g., extreme pressure, unusual reflectivity, bizarre atmospheric chemistry).

winning_patterns.evidence: A9Qa-RmuOr0 ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year') and similar temporal paradox hooks showed strong retention and engagement metrics.
winning_patterns.action: Use counter-intuitive time measurements or cross-species/planetary age comparisons (e.g., geological time vs. biological existence) in titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on standard psychological tricks (e.g., ef3ND4qiRHc, 5AN7LUgqarc) consistently underperformed in both views-per-day and overall interaction rates compared to space and extreme earth science.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-facts unless framed as high-urgency behavioral anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated basic animal facts (e.g., AXAfwrzzEdU, 1Bm0zw_qAAg on octopuses) showed declining incremental velocity in recent collection windows.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content toward cinematic survival, deep-sea horror, or prehistoric evolutionary oddities rather than basic anatomy listicles.
